questions.answer: As mentioned before, it was 100% successful when it comes to registration, however one course was not very clear about the prerequisites so it was more difficult to me than expected.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The styles are very similar. Maybe I got a feeling that there was less of a hierarchy and bureaucracy at my host institution, also the university was smaller and the classes more intimate

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: there were a lot of student associations available, including cultural, athletic and social activities. I myself joined a nature bathing association. But mostly I spent time with my new friends; we did chess tournaments, city tours, museum visits, bonfires and hikes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Discover local nature, architecture , talk to locals and get recommendations, watch art, make art<3

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Art and nature

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: the culture and language were very similar to those of my home town - so very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: be open and try to overcome the fear of losing control. remember that every person has something to teach you. remember to take your breaks; in the long run you have to be your own best friend, so this trust and listening to yourself is worth investing in.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: probably my host city was more polished

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The relationship to nature and the silence

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: free coffee at tenth floor in the math department! join a student association! investigate the student bars! be kind<3

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think the above covers it

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My self development, including fighting anxiety. Also improving my language and academic skills, getting to spend more time in nature. Making friends with people from around the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Overcoming myself

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Thank you again

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
